text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: multiple GPU nodes in us-west-2a reporting driver resets and container exits. Severity: P2 -> P1 if customer errors increase. Assigning oncall @maria. Logs show repeated Xid 31 and ECC uncorrectable events.

maria: I'm on it. pulling up node list and current pods. First priority: stop new scheduling to the affected GPU pool and drain flapping nodes.

sam: confirmed, I see 4 nodes in pool gpu-pool-1 with repeated restarts in the last 10m. Rough impact: ~6% increased error rate for realtime generation jobs and 1 customer reported 500s to support.

maria: cordoning the pool now:
```
kubectl cordon node-gpu-12.us-west-2a
kubectl cordon node-gpu-15.us-west-2a
```

maria: starting drain with evict for non-daemonsets (graceful):
```
kubectl drain node-gpu-12.us-west-2a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

infra-bot: action: nodes cordoned: node-gpu-12, node-gpu-15, node-gpu-21, node-gpu-22. Evictions started.

maria: collecting dmesg and nvidia logs from one of the failing hosts: pasted partial logs:
```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=4521, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: An Xid error has occurred. GPU may be hung
[ 1234.568012] EDAC MC1: CE page 0xabcdef80: ECC error detected, corrected
[ 1234.568110] EDAC MC1: UE page 0xabcdef90: ECC error detected, uncorrectable
```

sam: that UE line is worrying — uncorrectable ECC. Could be memory module or driver interactions causing page faults. We should try a driver reload on an isolated node first.

alex: agree. I'll take driver lead. If driver reload doesn't clear, schedule immediate hardware cordon (rack-level) and open ticket with vendor. For now try: modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia on a drained node, then run stress test.

maria: executing driver reload on node-gpu-21 (drained):
```
ssh ops@node-gpu-21
sudo systemctl stop inference-runtime
sudo modprobe -r nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia
sudo systemctl start inference-runtime
```

maria: after reload, the node came back up but kernel logged one Xid 63 before stabilizing. Running synthetic inference load for 5m to validate.

jamie: routing note — shifting live traffic off gpu-pool-1 to gpu-pool-2 and enabling CPU fallback for low-priority batch jobs to keep tail latency bounded. Updating routing rules now.

infra-bot: routing update applied: 12% traffic shifted to gpu-pool-2, cpu-fallback enabled for queue=batch-low.

support-engineer: customer impact snapshot — currently 1 paying customer (acct-9702) reported 500s for 2.5 minutes, about ~20 requests failed; internal dashboards show spike in 500s for realtime model route for approx 7m window. Drafting email: "We experienced transient GPU node instability affecting real-time model serving in us-west-2a. Mitigations applied; no data lost. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." Thoughts?

maria: good. include mitigation steps and recommended short-term workaround (switch to dedicated capacity or region). Mention that we have drained affected nodes and restarted drivers; latency normalized for most routes.

sam: ops update: 3 nodes required hardware-level cordon after repeated UEs. I've opened maintenance for them and flagged for vendor hardware triage. Remaining nodes in pool are healthy after driver reloads.

alex: kernel-driver note — we saw a pattern with 545.45 driver on these GPU SKUs. I'm testing a newer driver candidate 560.x in staging; if stable, we'll schedule a rolling upgrade tomorrow off-peak. For immediate mitigation we will pin model routing to pools with driver 560.x where possible.

maria: quick checklist for next hour:
- keep pool cordoned until hardware triage completes
- continue synthetic validation on recovered nodes (5m pass)
- escalate to vendor for ECC UE investigation (serial numbers attached in ticket)
- shift remaining burst traffic to other regions if saturation appears

jamie: placing an automated fallback: if error rate >3% for a route for >2m, route 40% traffic to alternate pool. Implemented.

support-engineer: sent preliminary customer notice to acct-9702 and to SOC for regulated customers. No data exfiltration signs.

maria: status update: after driver reloads and drains, two nodes remained unstable and are in maintenance mode. Error rate back down to baseline ~0.4%. Keeping incident open for vendor triage and driver upgrade validation.

sam: collecting post-incident metrics, will upload to incident doc. Early estimate: impact window ~09:12–09:20 UTC, peak errors at 09:14 UTC, affected capacity ~4 nodes (~18 GPUs).

alex: follow-up action items assigned to me: reproduce in lab, validate 560.x driver on same SKU, open vendor RMA if hardware fault confirmed.

maria: handing off to @sam for overnight watch and follow-through with vendor ticket. Oncall handover: I've recorded commands, node IDs, logs in the incident runbook. If anything spikes, escalate to P0 and page @alex.

sam: acknowledged — taking over. If error rate crosses threshold, I'll initiate region failover for impacted customers and notify support. Leaving notes in incident doc and tagging the hardware ticket.

oncall-bot: note: incident channel pinned runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1978001234 (record created).

maria: thanks team. Marking this thread as active; will add postmortem template once vendor findings arrive. :folded_hands:
